history.period: Late 19th / early 20th century; current structure 1960, renovated 1992
history.summary: CONFLICT (verify): accounts differ sharply on origins. One account says the temple was established in 1907 when the wrestler Alhad Singh Bhardwaj installed a Hanuman idol in an akhada in the then-deserted forests of Gumashta Nagar; a permanent temple building was erected in 1960 and an RCC roof added in 1992 (fifth-generation priest family of Pandit Bholaram Vyas, reported by Bhaskar English, 2025). Other travel-site accounts attribute it to Queen Ahilyabai Holkar in the 18th century. 'Ranjeet' (victory) is tied to legends that prayer here brings victory over adversity. A 'Ranjeet Lok' redevelopment (~Rs 7 crore, Indore Smart City) with Ramayana/Sundarkand motifs was announced in 2025.

name: Ranjeet Hanuman Temple
town_description: Indore, the largest city and commercial capital of Madhya Pradesh, is a historic former seat of the Holkar dynasty and one of India's cleanest and most food-famous cities. It is a major hub of temples and heritage structures on the Malwa plateau, served by an international airport and one of central India's busiest railway junctions.

travel.airport: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport, Indore - approx 12-15 km (verify)
travel.railway: Indore Junction - approx 4-6 km (verify); city buses, autos and taxis reach Footi Kothi Road
travel.road: On Footi Kothi Road, Gumashta Nagar, near Annapurna Road; well connected within Indore by city transport

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Hanuman Jayanti and Ranjeet Ashtami are peak days; Tuesdays and Saturdays draw the biggest crowds
